dedupe_keys.name: environmental impact of coherent point to multipoint pluggables in metro aggregation optical networks

description: Napoli, Antonio and colleagues document this resource in the B5G-OPEN community. The study computes device requirements and energy-related CO2 effects for horseshoe, ring and hub-spoke metro networks. It compares 400G ZR and ZR+ point-to-point modules with 100G/400G digital-subcarrier point-to-multipoint modules. Coverage comprises three modelled topology classes, not an observed national emissions inventory. The model reports fewer devices with P2MP technology. The abstract does not establish a full product life-cycle assessment or expose all energy/emissions factors. Zenodo provides the descriptive publication with open access; its stated licence is cc-by-4.0. Its publication licence does not establish a code licence or source-code availability. A limitation is that the native metadata do not establish all implementation settings, uncertainty bounds or independent reproducibility. Only descriptive metadata were inspected. Related records and companion papers retain their source-defined roles; they do not imply independent measurements.
